assessment: Chest infection, possibly early pneumonia on the right side. Patient is allergic to penicillin and has a family history of diabetes and heart disease.
objective: On examination, crackles were heard at the right lower lung base. Temperature was 99.4, blood pressure 138/86, and oxygen saturation 96%. Chest X-ray, complete blood count, and HbA1c test ordered. Patient is allergic to penicillin and has a family history of diabetes and heart disease.
plan: Start azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 5 days after food. Take paracetamol 650 mg if fever exceeds 102, not more than 3 times a day. Get chest X-ray, complete blood count, and HbA1c test. Switch metformin to extended release 500 mg once daily with dinner. Advise to drink plenty of warm fluids, take rest, and avoid sweets and sugary drinks. Follow up in 1 week with reports. Advise to rest for 2 days before returning to work. Instruct to stop hydrazine tablets and not take any medicine without consulting the doctor.
subjective: Patient Mr. Kumar presents with a two-week history of dry cough and night fever. He reports occasional yellow phlegm in the morning, mild breathlessness on stairs, no chest pain, and no blood in the phlegm. He stopped metformin due to stomach upset, continues amlodipine, and has a family history of diabetes and heart disease. He used to smoke but quit 5 years ago and does not drink alcohol. He has a history of penicillin allergy and a family history of diabetes and heart disease.
